original_idea.body:
# Causal Path from Benchmark Success to Real-World Harm: Where Is the Uplift Actually Generated?

**Problem:** AI labs use benchmark performance to assess harm potential, but the causal path from benchmark score to real-world harmful capability is not empirically documented.

**Direction:** For 3 publicly documented AI-assisted cyberattacks (GTG-1002 equivalents), identify which benchmark tasks correspond to the AI capabilities used. Measure current model benchmark scores on those tasks. Compute the benchmark-to-harm correlation. Identify which benchmark score increases most predict harm potential increase.

**Why it matters:** If harm potential is driven by specific benchmark dimensions, governance thresholds keyed to those dimensions would be more precise than current broad cybersecurity tier classifications.

**Relevant context:** OpenAI Preparedness Framework High threshold; Anthropic ASL-3/4 gray zone; Sarma & Fisher RAND on benchmarks as governance.
